title: Idgah
director: claude-opus-5-5 (authored in Claude Code, same rules as scripts/audio/direct.ts)

cast.name: Hamid
cast.description: Four-year-old boy, poor, thoughtful, quietly proud

cast.name: Mahmood
cast.description: Small boy, Hamid's friend, boastful and teasing

cast.name: Amina
cast.description: Hamid's grandmother, old, poor, loving, worried

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [warmly] Welcome to LitBridge, where stories cross languages. Today's story comes from the Hindi tradition. It was written in 1933 by Munshi Premchand, the father of the modern Hindi short story. It is called... Idgah.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [joyful] Eid arrives in the village after thirty days of fasting... and the children are the happiest of all. They count and recount their coins, because today they will walk to the Idgah, and then to the fair.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [softer] Hamid is the poorest of them. His parents are dead, though he believes his father has gone to earn money, and his mother has gone to bring gifts from Allah.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He lives with his grandmother Amina, who has managed to give him three paise. She worries all morning about letting such a small child walk so far, but she has no one to send with him.

lines.speaker: amina
lines.text: [worried] Hamid, beta... stay close to the other boys. Don't wander off.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At the fair his friends spend freely. Mahmood buys a clay soldier. Mohsin, a water carrier. Noore, a lawyer in a black coat. They buy sweets, and eat them slowly in front of Hamid.

lines.speaker: mahmood
lines.text: [teasing, mouth full] Mmm... want some, Hamid? Oh, you don't have any. [giggles]

lines.speaker: hamid
lines.text: [proudly] Sweets rot your teeth. And your clay toys will break by evening.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [tender] Then he sees a hardware stall... and a pair of iron tongs. He remembers his grandmother pulling rotis off the griddle with bare hands, and the burns on her fingers.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [amused] He bargains hard, and the tongs are his, for three paise.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the walk home, the other boys laugh at him.

lines.speaker: mahmood
lines.text: [laughing] Tongs? You bought TONGS at the fair?

lines.speaker: hamid
lines.text: [fiercely] My tongs are a soldier. They'll smash your soldier to pieces. No water carrier can stand against them!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [chuckles] Before the village comes into sight, their toys are chipped... and every boy wants a turn holding the tongs.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When Amina sees what he has bought, she scolds him.

lines.speaker: amina
lines.text: [scolding] Have you eaten nothing all day? You spent your Eid money on... on tongs?

lines.speaker: hamid
lines.text: [quietly] Your fingers burn on the tawa, Dadi. So I brought these.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [moved] And the old woman understands. She starts to cry.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [softly] In Premchand's telling, the little boy has played the part of an old man... and the old woman has turned into a child.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [gently] Idgah is a story about love that gives up its own small joys without a second thought. Thank you for listening to LitBridge.
